narrative.overview: A polished but restrained terminal interface that feels like a well-configured developer tool. Every visual decision serves clarity and density of information without crowding. The shell speaks through structure — box-drawing, aligned columns, meaningful prefixes — not decoration. Color is a signal, not ornament: a single accent for primary actions, semantic hues for state, muted grays for metadata. The default experience is monochrome and fully functional; color enhances but never gatekeeps.
keyCharacteristics: Structural over decorative: Box-drawing, arrows, brackets, prefixes convey hierarchy
Density with purpose: Information-rich but scannable; context appears when relevant
Restrained palette: One primary accent, semantic state colors, stepped neutrals
Graceful degradation: Full function without color; color only amplifies signal
Terminal-native: Embraces the character grid, monospace rhythm, instant transitions

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Deep Indigo appears on ≤10% of any screen. Its rarity is the signal.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Success/Warning/Error colors convey state only. Never used for decoration or brand.

rules.name: The Monochrome-First Rule
rules.body: Every screen is fully legible and functional in 16-color monochrome. Color is progressive enhancement.

rules.name: The Fixed Grid Rule
rules.body: No proportional fonts. No variable font sizes. The terminal character cell is the atomic unit.

rules.name: The Weight Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: 400 = body, 500 = contextual emphasis, 700 = structural headers and errors. No other weights.

rules.name: The 10-Char Command Column Rule
rules.body: Help command names occupy exactly 10 chars. Longer names truncate with …; shorter pad with spaces. Alignment is inviolate.

rules.name: The 50% Path Rule
rules.body: Working directory in prompt never exceeds 50% of terminal width. Truncates left with …/.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: Only the startup banner uses a full box-drawing frame. No other element frames itself.

rules.name: The Surface Rule
rules.body: Elevated UI (completion, history search, context badges) uses Surface background + Stone border. Base UI (prompt, output, help) uses transparent background.

rules.name: The Instant Transition Rule
rules.body: Terminal UI has no animation. State changes are immediate. Reduce-motion is inherent.

dos: Do use box-drawing (=, │, ┌, ┐, └, ┘) only for the startup banner frame.
Do use square brackets ([, ]) for inline context badges (git, venv, exit code).
Do align help command names to exactly 10 characters. Truncate with … or pad with spaces.
Do truncate prompt path at 50% terminal width, left-truncating with …/.
Do prefix every error with command:  in bold (Oxblood when colored).
Do indent error detail lines by exactly 2 spaces.
Do use Primary (Deep Indigo) only for: prompt symbol >, active completion row, history search, version in banner.
Do use semantic colors (Success/Warning/Error) only for state — never for decoration.
Do render all UI fully functional in 16-color monochrome. Color is progressive enhancement.
Do keep completion menu to max 10 rows with scroll indicator.
Do use Surface background + Stone border for all elevated UI (completions, history search, context badges).
donts: Don't use rounded corners or Unicode box-drawing with curves — terminal grid is sharp.
Don't add decorative colors, gradients, or background washes.
Don't frame command output, help sections, or error blocks — only the banner frames.
Don't exceed 10% Primary color coverage on any screen.
Don't use Success/Warning/Error colors for non-state purposes (e.g., don't color command names in help).
Don't animate, fade, or transition any UI element. Terminal changes are instant.
Don't show a cursor/pointer in completion menu — highlight the whole row.
Don't wrap command names in help — truncate at 10 chars with ….
Don't use proportional fonts, variable font sizes, or letter-spacing outside defined scale.
